To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we present the first linear-time algorithm to tetrahedrize the region between any two nested convex polyhedral regions, (b) our algorithm runs in O(n+m)3 log n+m time and (c) our algorithm produces 2(n+m-3) tetahedra.
we have designed an algorithm to tetrehedralize the region of a convex polyhedron and a convex hull in O((n + m)3log(n + m)) time.
we present an efficient algorithm to tetrahedrally decompose the volume between two convex polyhedra, and that we answer an open problem raised by the previous work.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of finding the minimum number of tetrahedralizations for the given two nested convex polyedra and the problem of finding an algorithm to construct such tetrahedralizations.
the problem of finding a set of tetrahedron which covers the region bounded by two nested convex polyhedral.

two important questions: 1) whether or not one can avoid Steiner points in the tetrahedralization of two convex polyhedra? and 2) whether or not the number of tetrahedral elements is linear in terms of the number of vertices of the two given polyhedral domains?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the region between two convex polyhedra can be tetrahedralized into linear number of non-degenerated tetrahedra by introducing Steiner points.
the problem of computing the tetrahedralization of the region between two convex polyhedra is NP-hard, and there are algorithms for the case of convex polyhedra with linear number of tetraherda.
the tetrahedralization of two nested convex polyedra can be performed in linear time with respect to the total number of vertices in the input polyhedra, without introducing Steiner vertices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the tetrahedralization of a convex polyhedron with Steiner points can be done in O((n+3)3) time, and without Steiner points, it can be done in linear time.

we present a novel algorithm to solve the open problem of tetrahedralizing the region between two convex polyhedra, and our algorithm is the first algorithm to tetrahedrate the region between two polyhedra without using Steiner points.

we have developed the first algorithm to tetrahedrize the region between nested convex polyhedrons into a linear number of tetahedra, and the first algorithm for tetrahedralizing a convex polyhedron into O(n) tetrahedron, avoiding Steiner Points.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tetrahedralization of two nested convex polyedra is a linear time problem.
the problem of tetrahedralizing the region between two convex polyhedra has a linear upper bound on the number of tetrahedral elements and the number of vertices.
, in the presence of a nested polyhedron, one can tetrahedrally fill the region in linear time, avoiding the introduction of Steiner points.
